cards.name: Diffuse Glow
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Distort filter that makes the image look shot through a soft diffusion filter: a glow in the current Background colour (white by default) is spread through the image with see-through grain. Clear Amount decides how far down the tones the glow reaches: high values keep it near the brightest areas, while at Clear Amount 5 (the demo) even the darkest photo areas lift from about RGB 59 to 104 and the colours turn pastel, so the whole frame reads as a faded, grainy, milky haze. A dark Background colour gives a smoky haze instead.
use_for: dreamy, romantic or nostalgic poster and wedding-photo look with glowing highlights
fake bloom / halation on a video still or product shot for a soft-focus glamour feel
ethereal glow behind a portrait or event photo used as a backdrop for headline type
grainy faded-film texture when stacked as a Smart Filter at reduced opacity
a faded, milky pastel backdrop behind headline type (low Clear Amount washes the whole photo)
avoid: Hidden in Filter > Distort by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Forgetting the background colour: the glow takes the background swatch, so check it (set white for a classic bloom) before running it or the script.
Already bright, low-contrast photos: highlights wash out to flat white; raise Clear Amount or lower Glow Amount, or build the bloom from a Gaussian-blurred copy set to Screen for a cleaner result.
Small type or fine linework: grain and glow eat thin strokes; mask the effect off text.
CMYK, Lab, Duotone or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert a copy first.
keeping shadows and contrast: at Clear Amount 5 the glow lifted the whole image, shadows included, into a milky haze; raise Clear Amount (15 default) to keep the glow nearer the highlights

params.name: graininess
params.does: Graininess: amount of see-through noise sprinkled through the glow
params.typical: 6 default; 0 for a clean glow, 6-10 for a gritty film look

params.name: glowAmount
params.does: Glow Amount: strength and spread of the background-colour glow in the light areas
params.typical: 10 default; 5-15

params.name: clearAmount
params.does: Clear Amount: how much of the image is left clear of glow; higher keeps the glow to the very brightest areas
params.typical: 15 default; 5 washes the whole frame into a milky pastel haze (plate render); 15-20 keeps the glow nearer the highlights

cards.name: Displace
cards.summary: Shifts every pixel sideways and up/down by an amount read from a separate displacement-map PSD: mid grey leaves a pixel in place, darker and lighter values push it one way or the other (first map channel = horizontal, second = vertical), so the image appears to wrap over the map's folds, bricks, fabric or ripples. Without a map file it cannot run; the harvest did not execute it because a headless call with no map wedged Photoshop.
use_for: wrapping a flag, logo or type onto fabric folds, crumpled paper, a brick wall or a T-shirt mock-up (map = blurred greyscale copy of the surface)
water / heat-haze / glass refraction using a ripple or noise texture as the map
glitch and slice offsets with a map of hard horizontal grey bands
conforming a pattern or texture to a body or product surface in compositing
avoid: Running it with no map file, headless: the harvest call wedged Photoshop for 128 s and left every command 'not currently available' until a restart. Always pass displaceFile pointing to an existing flattened .psd.
The map must be a saved Photoshop (.psd) file, not the open layer itself; save a blurred greyscale copy first (sharp maps give torn, jagged results; blur the map 2-10 px).
Large scale values tear the image and smear edge pixels; keep 5-20 for conform-to-surface work and choose Repeat Edge Pixels for photos.
If you only need a regular wave or a random ripple, Filter/Distort/Wave or Filter/Distort/Ripple need no map file.

params.name: horizontalScale
params.does: Horizontal Scale %: how far the map's first channel pushes pixels left/right; range not harvested
params.typical: 5-20 for wrapping, 50+ for glitch

params.name: verticalScale
params.does: Vertical Scale %: how far the map pushes pixels up/down (second channel, or the only channel of a greyscale map); range not harvested
params.typical: same as horizontal for an even wrap

params.name: displacementMap
params.does: Displacement Map: how a map of a different size is fitted to the layer
params.typical: stretchToFit for a surface photo; tile for a small repeating texture

params.name: undefinedArea
params.does: Undefined Areas: what fills edges that pixels moved away from
params.typical: repeatEdgePixels for photos; wrapAround for seamless patterns

params.name: displaceFile
params.does: Path to the displacement-map .psd (required)
params.typical: a flattened greyscale .psd blurred 2-10 px

cards.name: Glass
cards.summary: Filter Gallery Distort filter that makes the image look as if seen through a pane of textured glass: the picture is refracted by a texture (frosted, glass blocks, tiny lenses or canvas), so edges break up into wobbly, bumpy shapes while the colours stay the same. Distortion sets how far pixels shift, Smoothness how rounded the refraction is, Scaling the size of the glass pattern.
use_for: frosted bathroom / privacy glass look over a photo behind headline type
glass-block window effect for a retro or architectural poster
obscuring faces or details while keeping colours and composition (a stylish alternative to pixelate)
textured background plate for an event or social graphic
avoid: Hidden in Filter > Distort by default (harvest menu_visible false): reach it through Filter/Filter Gallery, a script, or Preferences > Plug-ins > Show all Filter Gallery groups and names.
Text that must stay readable: even low Distortion breaks letter edges; mask it off or apply under the type.
Very large images: Scaling tops out at 200 (harvested max), so at 4K+ the pattern can read as fine noise; raise Scaling or work on a downsized copy.
Brick, Burlap and Sandstone in the textureType enum are the shared Texturizer textures; the Glass dialog offers Blocks, Canvas, Frosted and Tiny Lens, so stick to those.
CMYK, Lab, Duotone or other modes: the harvest lists only Grayscale and RGB as supported, so convert a copy first.

params.name: scaling
